test_documents.content: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) is an object storage service offering 99.999999999% (11 9s) of data durability. S3 provides several storage classes designed for different access patterns. S3 Standard is designed for frequently accessed data. S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) is for data that is accessed less frequently but requires rapid access when needed. S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval provides low-cost storage for data that is accessed once or twice per quarter, with retrieval times ranging from minutes to several hours. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost storage class, designed for long-term retention of data that is accessed rarely, with standard retrieval times within 12 hours.

Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) enables you to launch AWS resources in a logically isolated virtual network. Subnets are subdivisions of a VPC IP address range. Security Groups act as a virtual firewall for your EC2 instances to control incoming and outgoing traffic. Security Groups are stateful: if you send a request from your instance, the response traffic for that request is allowed to flow in regardless of inbound security group rules. Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) act as a firewall for controlling traffic in and out of one or more subnets. Unlike Security Groups, NACLs are stateless: return traffic must be explicitly allowed by rules in the reverse direction.
